title: Filtering is off-policy too: what dynamic sampling removes, by task type, over time
purpose: Report what the filter removes by task type for every batch, turn the filter on and off, and evaluate on an unfiltered held-out set. The point of the design is that a filter is a policy: its rates drift, and they have to be watched.

steps.display: kubectl apply -f filtering-s06.yaml   # an Indexed Job on the research queue: 2 cells, 2 at a time
steps.output:

mean tokens that carry gradient per micro-batch: 5371 with the filter off, 3112 with it on

checks.description: both runs completed and each batch reported what the filter would remove, by task type
checks.because: Every time the trainer generates a batch it counts, per task type, the answer groups whose answers all scored the same. Such a group carries no advantage, so it teaches nothing.

checks.description: the filter drops exactly the groups the report counts
checks.because: With the filter on, the rows of a zero-variance group are masked out of the loss. The kept fraction recorded with the batch must equal one minus the dropped share; a difference would mean the filter and the report disagree.

checks.description: the filter changes what the run trains on: fewer tokens carry gradient with the filter on
checks.because: Masked rows contribute no tokens to the loss, so the mean number of gradient-carrying tokens per micro-batch falls by about the dropped share. This is the 'masked fraction is a cost' remark of the design: those answers were generated for nothing.

checks.description: the drop rate is not constant: for at least one task type it moved by five points or more between the first and the last quarter of training
checks.because: As the model learns, easy problems become all-correct and are dropped, hard ones leave the all-wrong state. The filter's effective policy changes with the model's, which is why the report is per task type and over time.

checks.description: the held-out set is unfiltered and identical for both runs (same problems, all three task types present)
checks.because: Both runs start from the same weights and are evaluated on the same 200 test problems with the same sampling seed, so their starting scores agree to the digit, and the evaluation applies no filter.
